Dataset

Upload a spreadsheet (.xlsx / .xlsm) straight from your computer — no SharePoint or database needed. We read one worksheet (the first, or one you name), infer data-quality rules from it, and score it across the DAMA dimensions just like any other dataset. If your workbook has several tabs, pick which one to assess below.

No file selected.
Excel workbooks can hold several sheets; name one (or its position, e.g. 2) or leave blank to assess the first.
Randomly samples this many rows. Empty — or larger than the file — assesses everything.
Dimension weights (optional)

Higher weight = the dimension counts more toward the overall score; 0 excludes it. Range 0–5; defaults shown.

Accuracy & integrity rules (optional)

Added on top of the auto-detected rules, so nothing else is lost. Leave empty to skip.

Accuracy lookups

A column and its full set of allowed values — anything outside the list counts as inaccurate.

Referential integrity

A column whose values must exist in a reference file — upload the reference and it's stored with this run.

idle 1. Request upload

What we check

Nine dimensions from DAMA & ISO/IEC 25012, weighted into a single score. Select one to see what it means.

Amazon Redshift Beta

Point us at a Redshift table. Via the Data API and a cross-account IAM role, the assessment runs as SQL inside Redshift — only aggregate results (and up to 50 sample failing rows per check) come back. Your data is never copied out, and full tables are profiled (no 100k sampling cap).

Assessment

Amazon S3 file Beta

Point us at a single object (Parquet, CSV, JSON/NDJSON or QVD). A same-account bucket needs only the URI; a cross-account bucket needs a role ARN or read-only access keys.

Assessment

Snowflake Beta

Read a Snowflake table with a read-only role. Checks push down as SQL so only results return.

Assessment

Databricks Beta

Read a Unity Catalog / SQL-warehouse table via a personal access token.

Assessment

PostgreSQL Beta

Read a Postgres table with a read-only user. The endpoint must be reachable from our worker.

Assessment

MySQL Beta

Read a MySQL table with a read-only user. In MySQL the database is the schema. The endpoint must be reachable from our worker.

Assessment

SQL Server Beta

Read a SQL Server or Azure SQL table with a read-only login. The endpoint must be reachable from our worker. Note: T-SQL has no regex before SQL Server 2025, so pattern/format validity checks are skipped — every other DAMA dimension is assessed in full.

Assessment

Azure Synapse Beta

Read a table from an Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pool with a read-only SQL login. The host is your workspace SQL endpoint (<workspace>.sql.azuresynapse.net), reachable from our worker. Synapse speaks T-SQL, so — as with SQL Server — pattern/format validity checks are skipped; every other DAMA dimension is assessed in full.

Assessment

Google BigQuery Beta

Assess a BigQuery table in place via SQL pushdown. Authenticate with a service-account key JSON that has BigQuery Data Viewer + BigQuery Job User on the project. The key is applied server-side and never stored in the browser.

Assessment

SharePoint / OneDrive Preview

Assess a file (Excel / CSV / …) stored in SharePoint or OneDrive. Our worker fetches it via Microsoft Graph using an Entra app registration (app-only). Your IT admin needs to register an app with Graph Sites.Read.All + Files.Read.All (admin-consented) and a client secret. The secret is applied server-side and never stored in the browser.

Assessment

Google Cloud Storage Beta

Assess a file (Parquet / CSV / JSON / Excel / …) stored in a Google Cloud Storage bucket. Our worker downloads the object using a service-account key with read access (Storage Object Viewer on the bucket). The key is applied server-side and never stored in the browser.

Assessment

Azure Blob / ADLS Beta

Assess a file (Parquet / CSV / JSON / Excel / …) stored in Azure Blob Storage or ADLS Gen2. Our worker downloads the blob using a storage connection string (it carries the account name + key — the single complete credential). It is applied server-side and never stored in the browser.

Assessment

Accuracy & referential integrity (optional)

Added on top of the auto-detected rules for this run — leave empty to skip. Lights up the Accuracy and Referential Integrity dimensions.

Assess by tag

Run a data-quality assessment on every source dataset carrying a tag — Redshift, S3, Snowflake and the rest — together in a single task. Ideal for scoring a whole domain (e.g. finance) across all its sources at once. Qlik-app tables, uploaded files, and any dataset without a saved connection are skipped.

🔑 Each dataset is assessed using its stored credential profile. A dataset with no saved credentials won't run — it'll be listed below with the reason. Qlik-app tables and uploaded files are also skipped. Tags are added on the Overview tab.

Frameworks & standards assessed against
  • DAMA UK (2013) — Six Primary Dimensions of Data Quality
  • DAMA DMBOK2 Revised Edition (2024) — extended dimensions
  • ISO/IEC 25012:2008 — Data Quality Model
  • ISO/IEC 25024:2015 — Measurement of Data Quality
